# CLAIMs with `works` `governance-of-possibility`

*Works — A manuscript the record's claims are marshalled into. Membership says a claim is in the work; whether the record believes it is the status, and the two disagree (ADR-032).*

**Regulation as the Governance of Possibility** — the owner's manuscript, requested at U24 and U25 of the exchange "Explain First Contact RL" and drafted by ChatGPT on 2026-11-23 (A48, fleshing out A46): Identity, Slow Modes, and the Temporal Organization of Adaptive Industrial Ecosystems. Regulation governs which organizations an industrial ecosystem can attain, sustain and revise, not only conduct within it; identity stabilization is selective temporal filtering indexed to the timescales of the demands; and adaptive governance keeps the capacity to reorganize viable, which a model with matched present performance separates from present performance. Its argument is held mainly in the lines realizability, distributed-agency, will-organization, formal-apparatus and readiness.

| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v10 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions are needed for it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)) and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Active |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v5 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. The readings say aid does not leave it alone: it does the work the capacity is learned from. Moss, Pettersson and van de Walle cite Kaldor, that a state leaves aid dependency as it "learns how to tax". Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's 1999 model already has taxing experience built by revenue collected and decaying with time, and capacity kept lower the more aid finances. Moore says raising revenue keeps a state's machinery alive at the grassroots. Ostrom et al. find recipients losing skill and rebuilding plants they did not maintain, and Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock find capability stagnating under aid. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. | [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v7 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. | [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) v5 | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. Here learning by doing needs capacity already present, dC/dt = λPC(1 − C) − μC. With λ = 1, μ = 0.3 and τ = 1.5, a party alone keeps C = 0.7, and C below 0.276 decays to nothing. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Tapering such support is worse the slower it is: from C = 0.45 under support doing 95 % of the work, an abrupt cut recovers, a taper over 5 periods recovers, and any taper longer than 9.13 periods traps the party. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. That reconciles Azam et al.'s optimal up-front cut, made for substitutive aid, with the Kenya exit study's success with gradual exits in which participants already did the work. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
